### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/page.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via ComponentPropsMap (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/layout-dsl.mdx`  _(via ComponentPropsMap (symbol, a top-level const object))_

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via ComponentPropsMap (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via ComponentPropsMap (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via ComponentPropsMap (symbol, a top-level const object))_

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via ComponentPropsMap (symbol, a top-level const object))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/page.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **142** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c980d114d3bdde4b2b639650cb762687a8da41fa` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `873c77c7045d47c80aeb65465b96a3e11f8496e2` — the merge of head `3c7f4da05c3258c1427c4d8e4f5d314b947f9f3d` into base `c980d114d3bdde4b2b639650cb762687a8da41fa`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 873c77c7045d47c80aeb65465b96a3e11f8496e2 && git checkout 873c77c7045d47c80aeb65465b96a3e11f8496e2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c980d114d3bdde4b2b639650cb762687a8da41fa 3c7f4da05c3258c1427c4d8e4f5d314b947f9f3d && git checkout -B drift-repro c980d114d3bdde4b2b639650cb762687a8da41fa && git merge --no-ff 3c7f4da05c3258c1427c4d8e4f5d314b947f9f3d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c980d114d3bdde4b2b639650cb762687a8da41fa
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c980d114d3bdde4b2b639650cb762687a8da41fa` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

**Verdict: ACCEPT.** Not governed (`check-governed-merges --pr 23590`). 3 files, +533 / −2,398, 2,931 changed lines, under the 3,000-line line. Prose and ledger-note work with `Clause-②: no`, so no contract review is owed; this record is the review.

1. **Shape.** Draft PR. The first line is `Part of #23434`, and `Clause-②: no` sits at line start. `.changeset/23434-component-read-points-part-2.md` is a `@objectstack/spec` patch; the package's `files[]` ships both `src/**/*.zod.ts` and `liveness`.
2. **Scope against the claim.** Item 1 (group C) for the second half of `component.zod.ts` (base line 7228 to the end). The claim set the split rule before any code: over 3,000 changed lines, PRs under the line each, the last one carrying `Fixes`. The union is 7,395 lines, and `component.zod.ts` alone is 5,675. So the split runs by file range rather than strictly by item. Accepted.
3. **Seat readings, taken on this head and not copied from the report.**
   - **Code is unchanged.** I compared the parser-accurate token stream of `component.zod.ts` (TypeScript AST leaves, JSDoc excluded) at merge base `fa6a6085c0` with this head. Both have 22,324 tokens, with 0 differences.
   - **The ledger changes in one place.** A deep compare of `liveness/page.json` against the base finds exactly one changed path, `props.regions.note`. That note is byte-identical in parts 1, 2 and 3 (62,138 characters), so the parts merge in any order.
   - **Evidence resolves.** I sampled 12 of the 186 direct `objectui @SHA FILE#SYMBOL` references in the note, evenly spaced, and resolved each at its own objectui SHA: the file exists there and the symbol occurs in it. 12 of 12 resolved. The sample includes the three historical trees `db11afd496`, `2e818d0b51` and `31971ff1e2`.
   - **Merge.** `git merge-tree` against `origin/main` `744b73f53f` is clean.
   - **Prose.** I read a slice of the diff: each record keeps its claim about the renderer and points to `liveness/page.json`, row `regions`. Change markers such as "since objectui `ce991bd70`" stay.
4. **Accepted deviations.**
   - The full derived battery ran on the union and on part 3's head, not on this part alone (a declared narrowing). CI runs the full set here.
   - `check:platform-checklist` is red on the base: 7 ABSENT SYMBOL anchors into `packages/metadata-protocol` and `service-storage`, which this PR does not touch.
5. **Out-of-scope dispositions.** None from this part. Part 3 (#23591) carries the census remainder and the open questions.
6. **Landing clauses.**
   - (a) Every check is green or skipped by design: read at landing, after the skip roster answers OK.
   - (b) `mergeable_state` is clean at enqueue: read at landing.

### ① Derived judgments

Post-hoc review of PR #23590 (part 2 of 3 of PR-2 for card #23434), judged as if it were still waiting to enter the queue. Inputs: the card body and every comment (rulings `6165388570` and `6181034096`; dev reports `6168538808`, `6170782619`, `6183204136`, `6183710619`), the PR body and file list, the net diff `fa6a6085c0..3c7f4da05c` (3 files, +533 / -2,398), and the 43 check-runs on the head. Every reading below is a `git show` / `git diff` of fetched refs in this repo, or a `git show` / `git grep` of the sibling objectui clone at the cited SHA; nothing was built, run or re-run.

**Accept set: unchanged (right).** `packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts` with its comments stripped is byte-identical between `fa6a6085c0` and this head (211,301 characters each side, string literals kept), so no Zod shape, `.describe()` string, strict door, default, refinement, export or type changed. All 2,397 removed and 521 added lines sit inside `/** … */` or `//` comments (a line scan of the diff finds zero non-comment lines in either direction). The `ComponentPropsMap` registrations at the end of the file change only their inline comments.

1. The JSDoc text of `src/ui/component.zod.ts` from base line 7228 to the end (the rest of object-kanban, object-calendar, object-form, object-master-detail-form, object-map, object-gantt, object-tree, object-timeline, the row registrations), which ships as source (`files[]` in `packages/spec/package.json` lists `src/**/*.zod.ts`) and as the docblocks of exported declarations in `dist/*.d.ts`. Each record's substantive claim stays: the `object-kanban.quickAdd` accepted-and-dropped record (head 7245-7262), the object-map and object-gantt key-by-key records (8554-8608, 8789-8826), the object-tree flat-key record with its "restore neither rung" warning (8906-8931) and the object-tree record itself (8951-9023), the object-timeline read-point list (9363-9397). 2. `packages/spec/liveness/page.json`, `props.regions.note` (`files[]` lists `liveness`): the same 120-entry evidence list part 1 carries, byte-identical (sha256 of the note starts `bf5b96cec57d` at `4196cb921e`, `3c7f4da05c` and `be8657fa44`; `main` at `56b2612778` holds the same). The entries for this half are [55] to [117]; every entry is spelled by symbol, none by line number (ruling `6165388570` item 2). The row's `status`, `evidence`, `verifiedAt` and `evidenceScope` are untouched; `check:liveness` path-scans `evidence` and `producer`, not `note`, and `Spec property liveness` is green on this head.

No generated docs page changes (no `content/docs/**` in the file list; `check:docs` runs inside the green `TypeScript Type Check` job).

**Sentences that could now be false: none found.** Checked:

- The `object-kanban.quickAdd` record (head 7245-7262) now states the count claim in words: "`ObjectKanban` names neither half of the pair in code (2 occurrences each, both inside the two objectui#11234 comments …, against 11 for the sibling `onCardClick` in the same file)". Read at objectui `b9814b334`, `packages/plugin-kanban/src/ObjectKanban.tsx`: `quickAdd` 2, `onQuickAdd` 2, `onCardClick` 11. True. The same file mounts `KanbanBoardCore` (its line 1725) and not `KanbanRenderer`, as the record (head 7268-7277) and entry [61] say.

The evidence list asserts no liveness for them; the `retiredKey()` tombstones and the `OBJECT_FORM_LAYOUT_RETIRED` map are untouched (tokens identical); their group-R counterparts (`migrations/entries/retired-keys/18.ui__ObjectKanbanProps__quickAdd.ts`, `…ObjectMasterDetailFormProps__details.sortField.ts`, the form-layout conversion) are not in the file list, as ruling `6181034096` requires.

Read at objectui `b9814b334`, `packages/plugin-tree/src/ObjectTree.tsx`: `'view-data'` 2 occurrences, `'undeclared'` 1 (a comment). Entry [104] records `P#dataConfig (resolveRecordSourceConfig with the view-data arm)` and `C#resolveRecordSourceConfig (rung 1)`. True.
- The one counting-method sentence kept on purpose, "occurrences of that identifier in each `src/index.tsx`" (`object-tree.objectName`, head 9031-9041, the 0-against-3/3/3/4 reading), keeps its method in the source; the PR body says the counted files are in that member's entry, and entry [105] `object-tree.objectName` exists in the list.

**Comment- and ledger-note-only on the published surface: yes.** This part publishes changed docblock prose and one changed ledger note, and nothing else. The PR body's sentence "No objectui read point remains in this half" holds on the counts above: what remains in the file are the first half's records (removed by #23589) and objectui commit references that mark a change, which are not read points.

**Landing check (post-hoc):** the squash `5afa1e05a7` has exactly the `git patch-id --stable` of `fa6a6085c0..3c7f4da05c` (this part landed first, so it carried the `page.json` line). Nothing landed that this review did not read.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/23434-component-read-points-part-2.md` declares `'@objectstack/spec': patch` and carries `Clause-②: no`; the PR body's third line is `Clause-②: no`. Both are right. The packed tarball changes (`src/**/*.zod.ts` and `liveness` are both in `files[]`), so a changeset is owed and `skip-changeset` would be wrong; no accept set widens or narrows, so `no` with no arm is the correct declaration and `patch` is its level (`yes` would demand at least `minor`; nothing narrows). The changeset body says what the spec source stops carrying, as ruling `6165388570` item 5 asks. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.
